newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean president's son apologises over furore.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean president's son apologises over furore.

text.p: South Korean President Kim Young-sam's son on Monday apologised for causing a political storm amid opposition accusations that he peddled influence in a loans scandal and meddled in state affairs.
"I, Kim Hyun-chul, bow deeply to the people and apologise," he said in a statement. The president's second son said he would accept punishment for any wrongdoing, but he did not admit to any crimes.
"I wanted to help my father but as a consequence made the mistake of causing trouble to father and anxiety to the people. I am deeply repentant now," the statement said.

He said he "wept profusely" when he saw his father apologise on television last month over the loans scandal involving Hanbo Steel Co. The elder Kim also apologised over his son's implication in the affair, saying he took "moral responsibility" as a father, but he did not admit any wrongdoing.
State prosecutors exonerated Hyun-chul in a probe into Hanbo's collapse under $5.8 billion of debt in January. But the opposition slammed the probe as a whitewash and demanded a new enquiry.

Kim Hyun-chul said he was prepared to testify before parliament and would agree to a new prosecution probe into his role in the Hanbo scandal. "I will willingly accept any punishment if I was in the wrong," he said.
